note: Names the rules profile and the drawings of this project, so no project name sits in the Python files. Paths are relative to the repo root, except inputRoot, which is the folder of the real input files on this machine. schedules names the two past schedule workbooks that the level proof reads from the References folder under inputRoot. drawings holds one file name per role. baseplan has the plot faces and labels. masterplan is the current master plan drawing, the second source check reads it and config/second_source.json names its plot layers. previousMasterplan is the master plan it replaced, kept for reference and not read in the full run. villaBlocks is the drawing the villa block of each unit is read from. roadLayout is the road layout drawing, its road edges give the front of a row. xrefRoles maps the name of an xref file that is not on disk to the role of the drawing that stands in for it. skip lists the other drawings the full run does not read, each with its reason. referenceOnly lists the drawings kept for reference only, R06_0000 and R06_0001 saved on this machine, which no villa block reader may take, since the villa blocks come from villaBlocks, the Building Footprint (Bader, Q045, R300). The analysis block holds how the CAD analysis reads the drawings. Lengths are in metres. partyWallShare is the share of plot.long_side that a shared edge must reach to count as a party wall. endShare is how far from the centre of a row, as a share of plot.long_side, a shared edge must lie to count as the front or the back of the row. roadEdgeLayers names the layers of the road layout drawing that hold the road edge polylines. unitPlotTypes lists the client plot types of the baseplan labels that stand for a plot with a unit on it, so only those plots get an issue when no unit code is found for them (R69). It is a list of plot types and never maps a plot type to a unit code (R30). noRev6Match lists the cluster codes of the profile that are old client codes with no Rev 6 cluster, and every cluster written with one of them gets an issue (R75). blockClusters maps the name of a footprint block to the cluster code it hints at, a block that stands for 2 or 4 plots says those plots are one cluster and it never gives a unit code to a plot (R90). The unit code of a plot is its Excel unit and nothing else (R69). pairRule false keeps the mirror flags of the blocks out of the row split until the original and mirror convention is known (R70). pastJob names what python/plan_from_past.py reads to build plan.json from a past job (R81). schedule is one of schedules and sheet is its sheet. prototypes is the full path of a kept copy of the prototypes.json the Revit reader wrote on the past model, since a later reader run writes prototypes.json again. prototypeFolder is the folder of the KEO prototype files under inputRoot, the Revit 2021 files of the past job, kept as the source. upgradedPrototypeFolder is the folder of their Revit 2024 copies with the same file names (R109), the folder plan.json gives the placer. output is the full path of the plan file, outside the repo. parameters lists the shared parameters to write on each link, RRE_ZZ_SP_Prototype-FFL is never one of them. testHost names what the Revit test host of R103 runs on. model is the site model under inputRoot that each run copies to <name>_TEST-<code>.rvt next to it, by a file copy only, and order is the prototype codes in the order they are tested, one per run. imageStepMinutes is the most the image step of an image job may run (Bader, Q061, R302), Run-TestHost.ps1 writes it into the job. imageMarginMinutes is what the job may run on top of it for the open and the close of the model, several times what the NBH 03 file took, whose measures are in steps/investigations/round-addin.md (CHOSEN, Round ADDIN). The job total is the two together and the window limit 3 minutes more. sampleSeconds is how often Run-TestHost.ps1 samples the private memory, working set and responding of its Revit and the free memory of the machine (R310), every 5 s as the sampler of I28 did (CHOSEN, Round ADDIN). cimTimeoutSeconds is the limit of each of the two CIM calls of a sample, the free memory and the child list, so a WMI that hangs never holds the wait loop, 2 s against the 42 to 109 ms the calls took on this machine, and two calls at it fit in the 5 s of the checks (CHOSEN, Round ADDIN review). helperProcesses names the processes Revit started in the window of KG3, conhost left out since every console has one, any of which a later window may reuse as it did the LocalDB of Steel Connections in Phase 1. Those already running at the start of a window are listed with their private memory in run.json, since the child figures of that window never count them (R310). pastJob.baseplanPlots is plots.json of the CAD reader run on the baseplan, relative to the repo root, and its plot faces give each yard floor its plot (R111). floors names what the floor step of the placer places (R112 to R116). types gives the floor type names of each kind, generic, yard and ramp, and the plan builder, the placer and the check use only these. keyTypes gives an answer key of answerKeys the type names of a kind its model names otherwise, FFL for the Generic floors of the IME and IMF keys (Round ADDIN Phase 1, READ from their reads), and a key reads the kinds it does not name by types (R321). levels gives the level of each kind. plotParameter is the floor parameter that holds unit-plot, for example VD2-2441, on all three kinds. yardBelowFflM is how far the top of the yard sits below the FFL (Bader, 24 Oct). yardShareTie is the share difference under which two plots tie for one yard. yardMinShare is the least share the best face must hold, under it the yard goes to no plot and is listed (round 15b review). cadLinks holds what the links from CAD are measured with (R120 to R123). cutShareMin is the share of its Generic floor that the baseplan face of a plot must hold, a plot under it does not follow the baseplan cut and is listed apart in every comparison (R120). cutNeighbours lists the plots Bader added to the cut plots, the neighbours of the listed plots whose links or ramps follow the past cut of those plots, and they are listed apart with them (R120). caseParameters names the link parameters the CASE test of R132 compares the second letter with. floorWidthStepM is the step the plot width is rounded to when the Generic and yard outlines are grouped (R135). planOutput is the full path of the plan python/plan_from_cad.py writes, outside the repo next to the plan of the past job (R128). handCheck lists the folders a read job of R245 may open a test copy in, the prototype copies of the data book (round DATA-4). siteBuild holds round Z4 (R200 to R219): folder is the round folder outside the repo with snapshot, work, images and logs under it, template the Revit 2024 metric template a newSite job starts from, newFile the name of the new site file in work, null between rounds so a job that needs it refuses, zoneNbh the neighbourhood of the zone the round is for, answerKey the past site model under inputRoot with the other discipline models listed for inventory only and the code of its Revit 2024 test copy, lock the one window lock both sessions share, waitMinutes how long to wait before the next look, staleHours when a lock with no window process is old enough to delete, minFreeGB the free memory floor before a window, windowProcesses the processes that count as an open window, snapshot the data book files read in this round, roadSurfaces the LandXML exports of the snapshot asked in this order for the plot front level and snapM the edge snap of R157, as roadSurfaceOrder of the data book, coordinateStepM the step the internal origin is rounded to, parameterGroup the group of the new shared parameters, steepUnits the units whose ramp is Ramps 2% and whose El @ Entry takes the steep slope, rampDepthM the Rev 6 ramp depth by unit, bandsMm the compare bands, and key14 the floor parameters of the 1.4 past model that hold its design FFL and El @ Entry (R221), corner the most a road edge midpoint lies from a curb and how near the ramp outline must lie to a face edge to sit on it (R224), footprint the height over the lowest floor level of a prototype that counts as its ground, the overlap a flipped house must gain to flag the mirror and the slack a judged link may lie past the key (R227 to R229), and placeSettleMinutes how long free memory may take to come back over minFreeGB before no more prototype code is placed (R231). placerCheck holds the split check of R261 to R263: position and level each with bandsMm and passMm, the X and Y gap of a link to the key and the gap of the link Z to the key FFL, and dialects names how a key is read, plot by parameter or by the instance Name, datum none or the survey elevation, and floorTypes when its floors are of other types than floors.types. majority holds the share a rule must reach on the past plots to be strong (Round 17) pastAll names what python/past_all.py writes per plot of a past key (R269): linkParameters the link parameters, floorParameters those of the Generic floor of a Native key, and entryParameter the one of them that holds El @ Entry majority holds the majority rule of Round 17 (R270 to R276): strongShare the share a rule must reach to be strong, levelHoldMm how near a level must be to hold, entryRampM how far an El @ Entry parameter may sit off its own ramp top, groups the keys of each generation, codeFrom whether a group is read by its Rev 9 code or its own unit, slopeBands, depthBands and heightBands the bands of the factors, rampTypeClass the slope class each ramp type names, groupSlopes the slope each group is tested with for El @ Entry, sideShare the share of the plot depth two faces must share to be side neighbours, wholeFaceShare the overlap a Generic floor needs to be the whole face, parameterTests the link parameters tested, overrideDecisions the decisions whose misses go to config/overrides/roshn-makkah.json. answerKeys lists the answer keys of Round ADDIN and how their Revit 2024 copies are made (R312): folder is the copy folder under inputRoot, manifest the JSON file in it that python/key_copies.py writes, format the Revit version every copy must have by its bytes, jobPrefix the letter that starts the code of the siteUpgrade job of a key, before the letter of its IM code. codePrefix is what every key code starts with, IM, and one capital follows it, the letter the job code takes. zonePattern is the shape of a zone, kinds the kinds of a key, TU for the site models and SE for the structural ones. codeInName is where the copy name and the file name of the source of a key hold its code, {code} standing for it, so a name swapped between two keys is refused. Each key holds its IM code, zone, kind TU or SE, the source under inputRoot its copy is made from and the copy name, the name of its model in Revit All Zones. The IMC copy is made from the Zone 02 ARC original, the IMC key, and not from the zone2 IMC of Revit All Zones, which is the master of the floor scenarios (Q065). prototypeNames gives the parts every KEO prototype file name is made of, prefix, then the discipline, then -, the prototype code, suffix and a number, .rvt, with ARC the discipline of the prototypes of the plan (R313). Run-TestHost.ps1 reads them and writes them into every job that names a prototype file, and the guard of the test host takes them from the job. prototypeSets names the other prototype files an upgrade job may save as Revit 2024 files besides the ARC prototypes of the plan (R313): STR, the 13 structural prototypes the SE models of IMA and IMB link, from their 2021 folder into a folder of their own in upgradedPrototypeFolder, so the ARC prototypes the placer takes by code stay alone (Q067). discipline is the part of the file names after KEO, STR, and codePrefix starts the job code of each, S and the prototype code. keyPlans holds how plan_from_past.py --key builds the plan of an answer key (R325): wallEdgeM is how near the middle of a wall must lie to an edge of a generic floor for the wall to go to that plot, 0.3 m, since the walls of the IMC key sit 0.099 m (median) to 0.100 m (90th percentile) off the edge of their generic floor (Round ADDIN 2b, CHOSEN). entryHeightM is the band in metres the floor top must stand over the El @ Entry parameter of its generic floor for the value to be used, 0.0 to 1.5 m, since on the 7 keys every generic floor stands 0.05 to 0.8 m over it but 21, IMC 10 and IMD 4 whose value is 0, IMF 6 whose value is the placeholder 150.0 and IMD 1217, which stand 14.8 m to 174 m off it (Round ADDIN 2b review, CHOSEN). majority.groups.parsons names the 7 answer keys of Round ADDIN by their code in lower case, imc being the IMC key read in Round 17 and again from its 2024 copy, so each row of past_all.csv takes its job as its source (R326). majority.kindLeaveOut names, per kind of answer key, the decisions its rows are left out of: SE, the structural models of IMA and IMB, hold no level, ramp or yard floor of their own and their Generic floors carry the SE levels, so their rows never count for the ramp slope, El @ Entry, ramp front and its fall, the height, the steps or the yard (Q066, Round ADDIN 2b review). pastAll.scheduleKeys gives each pastSource of plots.csv the answer key whose job made that schedule, past job plan the IMC schedule by plan_imc_past.json and schedule IMD the IMD schedule, so past_all.py --schedule-entry gives El @ Entry of a schedule only to the key of its own job (R326). placerCheck.dialects.parsons reads an answer key as R325 builds its plan: each plot by the face its generic floor stands on, the plot number parameter of a link naming its floor, and no datum, since the 7 keys hold their levels in shared elevation. entrySpots holds how python/entry_spots.py looks for the spot elevations at the plot entrance (R327): radiiM the distances from the entrance point, the middle of the higher long edge of the ramp (R94), 0.5 m for a spot at that point and 6.0 m for the corners of that edge, which lie 5.0 m from its middle at the median on the IMC key, and cornerM how near a spot must lie to a corner of the entrance edge, 0.05 m as the spot check of R47 (Round ADDIN 2b, CHOSEN)
